# Why does ChatGPT recommend my competitors?

*ReachKit*

:::answer
ChatGPT names the brands it has seen most often in text it judges authoritative — reviews, guides, industry writeups. If your competitors show up there and you don't, the model leans toward them. It isn't personal and it isn't fixed: it shifts as the content it reads shifts.
:::

:::takeaways
- ChatGPT doesn't rank brands — it scores how well each one semantically fits the question asked, and answers with the highest-scoring names.
- Appearing often in authoritative, relevant text matters more than appearing often anywhere.
- A small change in how a buyer phrases their question can change which brands get named.
- Nothing on your own site tells you when a buyer asks AI and your competitor gets named instead of you.
- A free scan shows where this is happening in your market before you write anything.
:::

## Why does ChatGPT keep naming the same few competitors?

ChatGPT doesn't pick favorites — it answers with whatever brands its training text associated most strongly with your category. If a handful of competitors show up again and again in reviews, comparisons and guides, those associations get reinforced, and the model reaches for them by default.

This compounds. The more a brand is written about, the more confidently the model attaches it to the category — which makes it more likely to appear next time, in front of more buyers, which drives more writing about it. If your competitors got there first, they're not winning because they're better. They're winning because they're more written about.

## Does ChatGPT rank companies, or just guess?

Neither, really. It isn't scoring and sorting a list the way a search engine does.

> The model doesn't consciously "decide" which brands to suggest—instead, it calculates semantic relevance between your query and every potential answer it could generate, then samples from the highest-scoring options. ([trysight.ai](https://www.trysight.ai/blog/how-chatgpt-chooses-recommendations))

[trysight.ai](https://www.trysight.ai/blog/how-chatgpt-chooses-recommendations)

So there's no leaderboard to climb. There's only the question of whether your brand sits close enough, in the model's text-based understanding, to the question being asked. If it doesn't, it won't surface — no matter how good the product is.

## Is it about how many times my competitor is mentioned online?

Volume matters less than where the mentions appear. A few mentions in the right places can outweigh a pile of mentions in weak ones.

A brand mentioned once in an authoritative industry report might carry more weight than dozens of mentions in low-quality content, according to [trysight.ai](https://www.trysight.ai/blog/how-chatgpt-chooses-recommendations). That's a different game than classic SEO link-building. It means a competitor doesn't need to flood the internet with their name — they just need to be named correctly, in the kind of writing the model treats as credible: comparisons, how-to guides, buyer questions answered directly.

## Will I get a different answer if I ask ChatGPT the question differently?

Yes, often a completely different one. The model is sensitive to exact wording, not just topic.

Change a few words in your prompt, and you might get entirely different suggestions, notes [trysight.ai](https://www.trysight.ai/blog/how-chatgpt-chooses-recommendations). That means there's no single answer to fix — there's a whole spread of buyer phrasings, each one a separate shot at being named or left out. A competitor might win the phrasing "best tool for X" and lose "alternatives to Y," or the reverse. Covering one doesn't cover the rest.

## Is ChatGPT working off old information about my market?

Partly. The model's core knowledge is frozen at a training cutoff, so it reflects whatever was written and visible online up to that point — not this week's news.

For most versions of ChatGPT, this means the model's foundational knowledge reflects the internet as it existed at a particular point in time, per [trysight.ai](https://www.trysight.ai/blog/how-chatgpt-chooses-recommendations). If your competitor had more written about them before that cutoff, that head start is baked in. Newer pages can still shift answers over time, especially where the model is pulling in current web results rather than just its training data — but it's a slower climb than people expect.

## What kind of content makes ChatGPT start naming a brand?

The pattern is consistent: brands that show up positively in places the model treats as credible get associated with the category faster than brands that don't.

If a brand appeared frequently in authoritative contexts—mentioned positively in tech reviews, cited in how-to guides, referenced in industry discussions—those patterns create stronger associations in the model's understanding, says [trysight.ai](https://www.trysight.ai/blog/how-chatgpt-chooses-recommendations). Practically, that means direct answers to the questions your buyers ask — written plainly, hosted on a domain the model can read — do more than a press release or a generic blog post ever will.
